$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT IN estate-gates. That repository already carries a
declaration, the `runs` field, and its own invariant 18 says plainly that
nothing reads a repository to confirm it. It cannot: the only thing that
knows which binaries a repository builds is the repository, so a component
that was FORGOTTEN is invisible from outside by construction. vouchryx was
installable by nothing for nineteen hours on 2026-08-26 for that reason.
THE TWO BUCKETS ARE THE POINT. Everything under `checked` is proved against
this repository by manifest_test.go, in this repository's own CI, which has
the toolchain to build and RUN the thing. Everything under `declared` is a
statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`. A richer declaration
that is equally unverified would be worse than the field it replaces,
because it looks like more assurance and is not.

role.value: the delegation plane: RFC 8693 token exchange, and the revocation list every enforcement point polls
role.why: a sentence about purpose is not a property of the source

key_material.why: that a path holds a PRIVATE key rather than any other file is read off the name and the doc comment; nothing in the type system says it, and this repository deliberately never marshals it into anything serialisable (invariant 9)

a_launcher_may_probe_something_else.why: stack-up polls that rather than the health path above, and it is the better probe here rather than a mistake: /healthz returns 200 the moment the process is up, while the key set answering proves the service can do the one thing it exists for. Declared so a cross-repo check reads a decision instead of a disagreement.

role.value: the reference client: keygen, exchange, proof

not_a_service.why: it exits when its subcommand finishes. A heuristic that looks for a listener would agree today and would be wrong the day somebody adds a `serve` to it, so this is declared rather than sniffed.
